meta.notes: Node ids reserve future production voice take ids: mina_c01_<node>.ogg. No placeholder speech ships; missing takes are intentionally silent. Silence is a first-class option on every node that defines silence_goto. Trust-only costs use bookkeeping flags (agreed_with_record, defended_the_record, annotated_the_blank, comfort_offered, refilled_the_record) that are never resolution flags.

fs_open.line: It stopped when you made the captions literal. Thank you. That is the correct phrase — thank you. Although you paused out there before you knocked. I have the pause down as: CALLER PREPARING BAD NEWS.

choices.label: That's not what the pause was.
You caption people too? Not just the objects?
Your captions have all been accurate.

fs_people.line: Objects were practice. You walked in and the air over your head said: TECHNICIAN. TIRED. HERE TO SAY IT ISN'T FIXED. Two of those are wrong. I keep them anyway.

choices.label: Why keep captions you know are wrong?
What does mine say now?

fs_now.line: TECHNICIAN. LISTENING. UNUSUAL. The third word is new. I don't have a rule for it yet.

choices.label: What do you write when someone just stops talking?

fs_flatter.line: They are accurate. Every one of them. You're the first person to say so out loud — and notice how nothing moved. You confirmed the entire record and the room is exactly as wrong as it was.

choices.label: Then accuracy isn't the problem.

fs_silence.line: CALLER DECLINES TO STATE. There. Captured. You can't out-quiet me — I've been catching silences for twenty-two years.

choices.label: What happens if a silence stays blank?
That's not what my silence said.

fs_push.line: Blank is worse. Blank looks like I missed the important part. When someone goes quiet on me I still hear a verdict forming, so the pause has to say something.

choices.label: Silence isn't evidence of what someone thinks.
Then we should caption the silence more carefully.

fs_push_sil.line: Right there — you did it again. CALLER DECLINES TO STATE. I wrote it before you finished not-saying it. I always win.

choices.label: Silence isn't evidence of what someone thinks.
Then we should caption the silence more carefully.

fs_named.line: Not evidence. A pause, four seconds, contents unknown. I wrote 'verdict forming' on a blank four seconds and filed it as accuracy. I'll log your sentence verbatim. It's the first thing today I haven't had to fix.

fs_misread.line: More carefully. Yes. Smaller words, better guesses. I'll refine the annotation schema tonight. Thank you for taking the problem seriously.

rt_open.line: Fixed twice now. And it held exactly as long as someone was in the room with me, both times. I've started captioning you in real time — currently: TECHNICIAN. PATIENT. PROBABLY BEHIND SCHEDULE.

choices.label: Two of those are guesses.
That's fair. I am behind schedule.

rt_sil.line: CALLER DECLINES — no. You're doing it on purpose now. A deliberate silence. What's my annotation for 'on purpose'?

choices.label: Maybe it doesn't need one.
Two of your three captions are guesses.

rt_agree.line: I know you are. It's on your clipboard. You agreed with the record — people usually argue. And notice: the transcript grew one line and the room stayed wrong. Agreement does nothing here.

choices.label: Because accuracy isn't what's wrong.

rt_guess.line: TECHNICIAN I can see — it's on your jacket. PATIENT is a guess. BEHIND SCHEDULE is a guess with a clipboard. If I struck every guess, do you know how thin the record gets? Four words an hour. A person could fall through a gap that size.

choices.label: An assumption written down doesn't become a fact.
Thin and true beats thick and guessed.
You're right — a thin record is a failed record.

rt_guess_sil.line: You keep handing me blanks like you know I can't spend them. CALLER SAYS NOTHING. SIGNIFICANCE PENDING. ...Pending. That's new. I never leave anything pending.

choices.label: An assumption written down doesn't become a fact.
Pending suits you.

rt_thin.line: Thin and true. Charming. You've never been the gap in a record, have you. Never had your four seconds go missing while everyone in the room acted like the words were there.

choices.label: Your four seconds?
An assumption written down doesn't become a fact.

rt_refill.line: Exactly. So I fill. I'm glad one of you finally understands the stakes of an empty column.

choices.label: Wait — let's go back to what you can observe.

rt_afact.line: Say that again — no. Don't. I heard it. Transcribing from memory: assumptions do not harden into facts just because I wrote them in the observations column. ...Then most of my record of you is annotation. Most of my record of everyone is.

choices.label: When did the annotating start?
You said 'the gap' earlier.

rt_court_door.line: Realtime court reporting. Twenty-two years, certified, two hundred and sixty words a minute. Nothing got past me. People's futures went through my hands and I caught every word — that is not a metaphor, that was the actual job.

choices.label: What changed?
'Went.' Past tense.

rt_court2.line: My ears started editing. Consonants first — quietly, the way a room goes wrong. I sat closer. I bought monitors. I learned to read the judge's jaw. And one afternoon a man stood up for his verdict, the judge spoke, and my hands didn't move.

choices.label: What did the record show?
What happened to the man?

rt_man.line: Guilty. Everyone in that room heard it except me. He was always going to hear it from the judge, not from my transcript — nobody's future hinged on my four seconds. That is not the part that broke.

choices.label: What did the record show?

rt_blank.line: The certified record of the State shows a blank. Four seconds, under my name. I have read that blank ten thousand times and every time it says the same thing: SHE MISSED IT. That's the day blanks started talking, so that's the day I stopped leaving any.

choices.label: The blank never said that. You did.
You've paid for four seconds every day since.
One gap in twenty-two years. Your record was accurate.

rt_heart_sil.line: You're not going to tell me it was fine. Good. Everyone tells me it was fine, and I write FALSE COMFORT next to their names.

choices.label: It wasn't fine. It also wasn't a verdict on you.

rt_armor.line: One gap. A 99.996 percent capture rate. Thank you for checking my math. Everyone checks my math, and the math was never the problem.

choices.label: Then let's talk about what the record is for.

rt_heart.line: Four seconds. Blank. Under my name. If a blank can say 'she missed it,' a blank can say anything — so nothing in this apartment stays blank anymore. You've watched me do it all night. So. The space where my four seconds were. What am I supposed to put there?

choices.label: Silence, four seconds, speaker unknown.
Nothing. Leave it empty.
Whatever lets you sleep.

rt_ann.line: That is what it says now. Word for word. I have annotated the blank for years, and it has never once gone quiet.

choices.label: Then stop feeding it.

rt_safe.line: Sleep. The full transcript is how I sleep. It is also why I don't.

choices.label: The transcript isn't keeping you safe.

rt_told.line: There. LEAVE IT EMPTY — TECHNICIAN'S INSTRUCTION. You see the problem? The moment you say 'leave it empty' out loud, I write that down, and it isn't empty anymore. Try again.

choices.label: Try again how?

rt_earned.line: ...Nothing. You heard the question and you're not filling the space. Neither am I. Look at that. Four seconds — five now — six — and it isn't a verdict, it isn't a failure, it's just blank. Blank can be accurate. I'm leaving it. I'm actually leaving it.

rt_open2.line: Where were we. You were about to be useful, and I was about to write down what I decided you meant instead of what you said.

choices.label: Back to what you can actually observe.

int_open.line: Then let's leave one thing unexplained on purpose.

choices.label: [Leave a quiet beat.]

fb_open.line: The captions are still getting ahead of what actually happened.

choices.label: I'll keep the next pass strictly factual.

fb_sil.line: CALLER DECLINES TO STATE. Noted. Get back to work.

res_open.line: The kettle boiled twice this morning and said nothing about it. We're both letting that stand.
